topic: humanoid robot market: funding, manufacturers, deployments, IPOs, adoption

items.title: Booster Robotics debuts the T2, a humanoid built for research labs
items.summary: The 140 cm, 43 kg biped is pitched as Booster's flagship embodied-AI platform for universities and research teams, with 31 degrees of freedom, Thor T5000 compute and a claimed 7 km/h top speed, according to the company. Already in production, the T2 leans on navigation — stair climbing, 100-meter runs and recovery from falls — rather than fine manipulation.

items.title: UBTECH points the $25,000 U1 Pro at homes, not factories
items.summary: The 183 cm humanoid, up for pre-order at roughly $25,000, carries 88 degrees of freedom and an emotional language model called Resonance LM, targeting companionship, reception and light tasks like folding clothes, according to UBTECH. Sub-20-millisecond lip sync signals where the priorities lie: presence and interaction over heavy labor.

items.title: Unitree closes in on a $619M Shanghai IPO as the US ban lands
items.summary: The Hangzhou company is finalizing pricing on a STAR Market listing targeting 4.2 billion yuan (about $619 million) after what humanoid.guide calls the fastest sign-off in STAR Market history — a debut that would make Unitree the first humanoid robot developer on China's A-share market. With the FCC's import ban arriving just as Chinese listing preparations peak, Counterpoint Research reckons the timing is 'unlikely to be accidental.'

items.title: China vows to retaliate over the US robot ban
items.summary: China's commerce ministry says it will “resolutely retaliate” and safeguard its interests if Washington insists on the FCC's import ban on new Chinese robots and power inverters, urging the US to withdraw what it calls “erroneous actions” and “unilateral bullying,” according to Reuters. The warning turns last week's ban — which hits humanoid market leader Unitree hardest — into an open trade fight.

items.title: Robot industry splits over the US import ban
items.summary: Security hawks hail the FCC's block on new foreign humanoids as a defining technology-security move, while analysts warn it could slow US physical-AI innovation and may even catch Canadian and European robots, according to experts canvassed by The Robot Report. China has shipped 80–90% of the world's humanoids to date, per IFR figures cited in the piece.

items.title: The US bans new Chinese humanoid robots
items.summary: The FCC is barring imports of new models of Chinese humanoid and quadruped robots, along with grid-connecting power inverters, to shield the US AI buildout from disruption, data theft and cyberattacks, according to a Reuters exclusive. Unitree — holding roughly a fifth of the global humanoid market — is the most exposed name, though already-authorized models can keep shipping for now.

items.title: A $57,590 classroom humanoid sparks a New York backlash
items.summary: Realbotix's M-Series robot “Sally” and its Optio AI assistant are set to join a Salamanca High School classroom this fall — on Seneca Nation territory where about 40% of students are Native American — drawing opposition from teachers' unions and state education officials over privacy, data security and the role of human educators.

items.title: Generative Bionics debuts Gene.01, a smart-skin humanoid
items.summary: The Italian startup's first platform wraps a sensor skin from torso to limbs that detects people before contact and supports guide-by-hand training, according to the company. Built on Italian Institute of Technology research and an $81 million seed led by CDP Venture Capital, Gene.01's first job is welding work with shipbuilder Fincantieri.

items.title: Mitsubishi Motors teams up with Highlanders to mass-produce humanoids
items.summary: Mitsubishi Motors has partnered with University of Tokyo spinout Highlanders to develop and mass-produce AI-equipped humanoid robots, starting with trials on an engine line at its Kyoto plant. The pair are targeting output of 1,000 units a month by the end of 2027, according to the companies.

items.title: A push to ban Chinese humanoids reaches Washington
items.summary: A Daily Signal op-ed urges the FCC to put Chinese humanoid robots on its Covered List — the mechanism used against Huawei gear and DJI drones — casting camera-laden machines like Unitree's $13,500 G1 as mobile data-collection platforms, according to the authors, who cite over $20 billion in Beijing robotics subsidies. The call lands as Rep. John Moolenaar's NDAA amendments seek an assessment of U.S. military infrastructure's dependence on hardware from adversarial foreign suppliers.

items.title: Holiday Robotics breaks cover with FRIDAY, a hands-first wheeled humanoid
items.summary: Seoul-based Holiday Robotics has unveiled FRIDAY, a wheeled humanoid aimed at manufacturing, automotive, semiconductor and logistics work. According to the company, the robot packs 64 degrees of freedom — 40 of them in its hands — along with hot-swappable batteries and a vision-language-skill software stack now in private pilots with industrial partners.

items.title: Kalanick's Atoms raises $1.7B — and it's not betting on humanoids
items.summary: Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick has raised $1.7 billion for Atoms in a round led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Bain Capital and Uber participating, to build AI-driven robots and automation for manufacturing, real estate and transportation. According to Kalanick, humanoids will be good at low-scale tasks in human-designed spaces — high-volume industrial work will go to purpose-built machines.

items.title: Japan's humanoid push moves into factories and airports
items.summary: Japan Airlines is running a two-year Haneda Airport trial of Unitree G1-based humanoids for ground handling with GMO AI & Robotics, Toyota is evaluating prototypes on a components line, and Mitsubishi Motors is targeting 1,000 robots a month as early as 2027, according to humanoid.guide's roundup. METI is backing the push with roughly ¥90 billion a year in robotics support.

items.title: Tesla goes quiet on Optimus volume production
items.summary: Tesla's Q2 shareholder letter drops the previous quarter's language about the Optimus humanoid reaching volume production, according to TechCrunch — in a quarter where capital spending more than doubled and volume-production timelines for the Cybercab, Semi and Megapack 3 all slipped.

items.title: EngineAI opens a humanoid combat league in Shenzhen
items.summary: EngineAI's Ultimate Robot Knockout Legend kicked off in Shenzhen with 32 teams fighting full-size T800 humanoids — a roughly $40,500, 29-joint machine, according to the company — ahead of finals in November–December. The Chinese Institute of Electronics projects China's humanoid robot market will reach about 870 billion yuan by 2030.

items.title: UK's Humanoid raises $152M, calling itself Europe's first humanoid unicorn
items.summary: The London startup behind the wheeled HMND 01 closed a $152 million Series A led by Prime Movers Lab at a $1.35 billion post-money valuation — making it Europe's first pure-play humanoid robotics unicorn, according to the company. Schaeffler and Bosch join as strategic backers, doubling as anchor customer and contract manufacturer ahead of a Q4 2026 beta rollout.

items.title: Hyundai workers strike over Atlas deployment plans
items.summary: Around 35,000 unionized workers at Hyundai's Ulsan complex have begun four-hour walkouts demanding union approval before humanoid robots enter Korean factories — just as Hyundai completes its full takeover of Atlas maker Boston Dynamics. The partial strikes have reportedly already cut output by roughly 5,000 vehicles.

items.title: Verified deployments favor Figure and Agility
items.summary: humanoid.guide's mid-year review finds real industrial humanoid work still concentrated at a handful of named sites: Figure 02 logged 1,250+ hours and 90,000+ parts in its 11-month BMW pilot, while Agility's Digit has passed 65,000 operating hours across nine customer facilities, according to the companies.

items.title: UK's Humanoid puts HMND 01 on wheels for warehouse work
items.summary: The London startup is putting roughly 90% of its engineering into a wheeled version of its HMND 01 robot for shelf stocking and machine feeding — lifting 15 kg and working at about 80% of human speed, according to Humanoid, with CE certification targeted for late 2027.

items.title: AgiBot debuts four robots at WAIC, led by the A3 Ultra humanoid
items.summary: At Shanghai's World AI Conference the company unveiled the 1.74 m, 51-DoF A3 Ultra — running Nvidia's Thor chip with up to eight hours of runtime, according to AgiBot — alongside the X2 EDU education platform, the industrial G2 Max and the 20-DoF OmniHand 3 Ultra-M dexterous hand.

items.title: Weave Robotics puts the home humanoid on sale at $7,999
items.summary: The San Francisco startup has opened orders for Isaac 1, a wheeled home robot that folds laundry, makes beds and tidies rooms autonomously, according to Weave — $7,999 up front or $449 a month, with first deliveries this fall.

items.title: Hyundai moves to take full ownership of Boston Dynamics
items.summary: SoftBank is exercising its put option and Hyundai Motor Group shareholders will buy out its remaining stake in the Atlas maker, according to Hyundai — which says it plans to put Atlas humanoids to work at its Metaplant America factory from 2028.

items.title: LimX Dynamics closes a $200M Pre-IPO round at a RMB 15B valuation
items.summary: The Shenzhen humanoid maker has now raised $400 million in six months — days before showing its Oli robot clearing a room of household chores fully autonomously.

items.title: Toyota spinout Walden Robotics launches with $300M at a $1.1B valuation
items.summary: The Toyota Research Institute spinout led by MIT's Russ Tedrake emerged from stealth with backing from Toyota, Nvidia, Boeing and Samsung — and says its wheeled general-purpose robots have been working at a Toyota plant in North America since February.

items.title: Agility Robotics heads for the stock market at a ~$2.5B valuation
items.summary: The Oregon-based maker of Digit plans to list via a SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI, raising over $620 million — while CEO Peggy Johnson says home humanoids are still a decade out.

items.title: Amazon and Nvidia among backers of Neura Robotics, CNBC reports
items.summary: More Big Tech capital flows into the humanoid race as the German robot maker draws high-profile investors.
